Sources: [evoformer.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L46-L74)

## Phase 1: Pair Initialisation

### Sequence-Pair Embedding

The pair representation is bootstrapped from the target features via a **decomposition into left and right single projections**: `pair = Linear_left(target_feat)[:, None] + Linear_right(target_feat)[None, :]`. This produces a `[N, N, pair_channel]` tensor where each position `(i, j)` receives information from both token `i` and token `j` independently. A pair mask is constructed as the outer product of per-token masks.

### Previous-Cycle Embedding

In recurrent inference (up to 10 recycling iterations), the pair output from the previous cycle is injected via `LayerNorm → Linear` with the `global_config.final_init` initialiser. This residual pathway allows the trunk to refine its representations across cycles — the initial cycle passes a zero tensor, making this a no-op on the first forward pass.

### Relative Position Encoding

The `_relative_encoding` method calls `featurization.create_relative_encoding`, which computes four one-hot feature maps from the `TokenFeatures` metadata:

| Feature | Source Fields | Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Relative residue index | `residue_index` | Clipped offset, one-hot over `[−max_relative_idx, +max_relative_idx]`; out-of-chain mapped to sentinel |
| Relative token index | `token_index` | Same clipped-offset scheme, but only active within the same residue |
| Same entity | `entity_id` | Binary indicator `entity_id[i] == entity_id[j]` |
| Relative chain (symmetry) | `sym_id` | Clipped offset within entity, one-hot over `[−max_relative_chain, +max_relative_chain]` |

The concatenated features are projected to `pair_channel` via a linear layer and added to the pair activations. This encoding is critical for the model to learn distance-dependent and chain-dependent structural priors.

### Bond Embedding

The `_embed_bonds` method constructs a **contact matrix** from two bond sources: `polymer_ligand_bonds` and `ligand_ligand_bonds`. Each bond's token indices are gathered, validated against their masks, and used to set entries in the contact matrix. The resulting `[N, N, 1]` tensor is projected to `pair_channel` and added to the pair activations. This is the mechanism by which AlphaFold 3 communicates covalent bond topology (e.g., ligand-protein bonds, DNA-protein crosslinks) to the trunk.

### Template Pair Embedding

The `TemplateEmbedding` module processes structural templates through a `SingleTemplateEmbedding` (which runs a 2-layer `PairFormerIteration` over each template's distogram and unit-vector features), then aggregates across templates via scan summation. A **multichain mask** (`asym_id[:, None] == asym_id[None, :]`) restricts template features to intra-chain pairs, since templates are per-chain. The aggregated template activations are added to the pair representation.

Sources: [evoformer.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L86-L206), [featurization.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/featurization.py#L177-L257)

## Phase 2: MSA Stack (EvoformerIteration)

The MSA processing phase transforms the pair representation using evolutionary information from the multiple sequence alignment. The pipeline is: **shuffle → truncate → featurise → Evoformer stack**.

The MSA is shuffled with a padding-consistent Gumbel argsort, then truncated to `num_msa` rows. Feature construction produces a per-row tensor concatenating a one-hot encoding of the MSA residue types, a binary deletion indicator, and a scaled deletion value (`arctan(d/3) * 2/π`). The MSA activations are initialised as `Linear(msa_feat) + Linear(target_feat)[None]` — the target features broadcast across all MSA rows.

Each **EvoformerIteration** performs the following operations in sequence:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph EvoformerIteration
        OPM["OuterProductMean\nmsa → pair"]
        MSA1["MSAAttention\n(msa, pair) → msa"]
        MT["TransitionBlock\nmsa → msa"]
        TRI1["TriangleMult outgoing\npair → pair"]
        TRI2["TriangleMult incoming\npair → pair"]
        PA1["GridSelfAttention\npair → pair"]
        PA2["GridSelfAttention (T)\npair → pair"]
        PT["TransitionBlock\npair → pair"]
        OPM --> MSA1 --> MT --> TRI1 --> TRI2 --> PA1 --> PA2 --> PT
    end
```

| Sub-module | Input → Output | Key Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **OuterProductMean** | msa `[S,N,C_m]` → pair `[N,N,C_z]` | Projects MSA rows to left/right channels, computes chunked einsum outer product, normalises by mask product |
| **MSAAttention** | msa + pair → msa | Pair-conditioned attention: softmax over pair-derived logits aggregates MSA values across rows, with gating |
| **TriangleMultiplication** (×2) | pair → pair | Outgoing (`ikc,jkc→ijc`) and incoming (`kjc,kic→ijc`) triangle updates with GLU gating |
| **GridSelfAttention** (×2) | pair → pair | Row-wise and column-wise self-attention (transpose=True for columns) with pair bias and flash attention |
| **TransitionBlock** (×2) | msa → msa, pair → pair | Two-layer MLP with Swish-gated linear unit (GLU) and 4× expansion factor |

All updates are **residual** — each sub-module's output is added to its input. The MSA and pair representations evolve jointly through this block, enabling information to flow from evolutionary statistics (MSA) into pairwise structural constraints and vice versa. After the final EvoformerIteration, only the **pair output** is retained; the MSA representation is discarded.

Sources: [modules.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L542-L633), [evoformer.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L208-L250)

## Phase 3–4: Pairformer Stack

After the MSA stack completes, the **single representation** is initialised as `Linear(target_feat) + Linear(LayerNorm(prev_single))`, mirroring the pair initialisation pattern. The Pairformer stack then jointly refines both representations.

Each **PairFormerIteration** (with `with_single=True`) performs:

| Step | Operation | Tensor Shape |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | TriangleMultiplication (outgoing) | `[N,N,C_z] → [N,N,C_z]` |
| 2 | TriangleMultiplication (incoming) | `[N,N,C_z] → [N,N,C_z]` |
| 3 | GridSelfAttention (row-wise) | `[N,N,C_z] → [N,N,C_z]` |
| 4 | GridSelfAttention (column-wise) | `[N,N,C_z] → [N,N,C_z]` |
| 5 | TransitionBlock (sharded) | `[N,N,C_z] → [N,N,C_z]` |
| 6 | Single Attention with pair bias | `[N,C_s] → [N,C_s]` |
| 7 | Single TransitionBlock | `[N,C_s] → [N,C_s]` |

The **single attention** mechanism is a key architectural detail: the pair representation is projected to pair logits via `Linear(LayerNorm(pair))`, which serve as a position-dependent bias for the self-attention over the single representation. This allows the pairwise structural information accumulated through 48 Pairformer layers to directly modulate the per-token embeddings. The pair logits are transposed to `[num_heads, N, N]` and passed to `diffusion_transformer.self_attention` alongside the sequence mask.

The pair transition block supports **sharded application** — controlled by `shard_transition_blocks` and `pair_transition_shard_spec` in the global config — which splits the transition computation along the token dimension to manage memory pressure on large inputs.

Sources: [modules.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L422-L539)

## Core Sub-Modules Deep Dive

### TransitionBlock

A gated two-layer MLP: `LayerNorm → GLU(Swish) → Linear`. The GLU kernel uses `tokamax.gated_linear_unit` for fused computation when `use_glu_kernel=True`, decomposing the intermediate projection into gate and value branches (`Swish(a) * b`). The expansion factor defaults to 4×, controlled by `num_intermediate_factor`.

### TriangleMultiplication

Implements the geometric triangle update — the signature operation that gives Evoformer its name. Two variants exist:

| Variant | Equation | Geometric Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outgoing | `ikc,jkc→ijc` | Information flows along edges sharing a source vertex `i` |
| Incoming | `kjc,kic→ijc` | Information flows along edges sharing a target vertex `j` |

Both apply `LayerNorm → GLU projection → split into a,b → einsum → LayerNorm → Linear → sigmoid gate`. The GLU kernel fuses the projection and gating for efficiency.

### GridSelfAttention

Row-wise or column-wise (transpose) self-attention over the pair representation. Uses `tokamax.dot_product_attention` with flash attention implementation selection. The query/key/value projections use transposed weights for the Q and K branches. A pair bias term from the linear projection of the input is added to attention logits. The output is gated by a sigmoid-linear projection of the input. The computation is wrapped in `inference_subbatch` for chunked processing at inference time.

### MSAAttention

Pair-conditioned attention across the MSA rows dimension: softmax over pair-derived logits `[H, N, N]` aggregates MSA values `[S, N, C]` across the sequence dimension `S`, producing a weighted average that blends evolutionary statistics with pairwise structure. The key insight is that the pair representation controls which positions each MSA row attends to, creating a feedback loop between structural and evolutionary information.

### OuterProductMean

Projects MSA activations to left and right channels of dimension `num_outer_channel` (default 32), then computes the mean outer product via a chunked einsum `abc,ade,cef→bdf` with a learned weight tensor `[C_outer, C_outer, C_z]`. The result is normalised by the outer product of masks (`ε + mask^T @ mask`), ensuring well-defined output even for heavily padded MSAs.

Sources: [modules.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L50-L419)

## Recycling Loop

The Evoformer Trunk is invoked within a recycling loop in the `Model.__call__` method. The loop runs for `num_recycles + 1` iterations (default 11 total: 1 initial + 10 recycling). On each iteration:

1. The previous cycle's `single` and `pair` embeddings are injected via the `_prev_embedding` and `_prev_single_embedding` pathways (zero on the first iteration).
2. The Evoformer Trunk produces new embeddings.
3. Embeddings are cast to `float32` for numerical stability before the next cycle.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant M as Model
    participant E as Evoformer Trunk
    participant D as DiffusionHead

    M->>E: "Cycle 0: prev={zeros}"
    E-->>M: "{single₀, pair₀}"
    M->>E: "Cycle 1: prev={single₀, pair₀}"
    E-->>M: "{single₁, pair₁}"
    Note over M: ... (10 recycling iterations)
    M->>E: "Cycle 10: prev={single₉, pair₉}"
    E-->>M: "{single₁₀, pair₁₀}"
    M->>D: "embeddings={single₁₀, pair₁₀}"
```

During `hk.running_init()` (parameter initialisation), only a single forward pass is executed to avoid excessive compile time. At inference, `hk.fori_loop` enables efficient XLA-compiled recycling.

Sources: [model.py](src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L289-L319)

## Bfloat16 Precision Context

The entire Evoformer Trunk forward pass executes within a `bfloat16_context()` manager, controlled by `global_config.bfloat16`. When set to `'all'`, all activations and computations use `bfloat16` for throughput on TPUs, with explicit `float32` casting of the output embeddings at the recycling boundary. The `assert self.global_config.bfloat16 in {'all', 'none'}` guard at the trunk's entry point enforces that only these two precision modes are valid.

Sources: [evoformer.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L260-L269)

## Target Feature Embedding

Before entering the Evoformer, the `target_feat` is constructed by concatenating two sources: (1) token-level features from `featurization.create_target_feat` (one-hot residue type, MSA profile, deletion mean) and (2) per-atom conditioning from `atom_cross_attention.atom_cross_att_encoder`. The per-atom conditioning runs a 3-block AtomTransformer over the atom-level features, producing a token-level summary that encodes local atomic geometry (element types, reference positions, atom masks). This fusion of token-level and atom-level information at the input is unique to AlphaFold 3 and enables the model to reason about ligand geometry from the very first layer.

Sources: [model.py](src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L152-L180)

## Output Contract

The Evoformer Trunk returns a dictionary with three keys:

| Key | Shape | Dtype | Consumer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `single` | `[N, 384]` | bfloat16 or float32 | DiffusionHead, ConfidenceHead, DistogramHead |
| `pair` | `[N, N, 128]` | bfloat16 or float32 | DiffusionHead, ConfidenceHead, DistogramHead |
| `target_feat` | `[N, D_target]` | as computed | ConfidenceHead |

Shape assertions at lines 342–348 verify the output dimensions match the configured `pair_channel` and `seq_channel`, serving as compile-time guards against configuration errors.

> [!TIP]
> The 48-layer Pairformer stack is the computational bottleneck of the trunk. The `block_remat` and `remat_block_size` parameters in `PairformerConfig` control rematerialisation granularity — setting `block_remat=True` with `remat_block_size=8` checkpoints every 8 layers, trading 12.5% recomputation for approximately 8× reduction in peak activation memory during backpropagation.

> [!TIP]
> The MSA representation is discarded after the Evoformer stack — only the pair output survives. This design choice means the Pairformer's 48 layers operate purely on pair+single representations, eliminating the `[S, N, C_m]` MSA tensor from memory during the deepest and most parameter-intensive phase of the trunk.

Sources: [evoformer.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L342-L356)

## Navigation

- **Upstream**: The Evoformer consumes features produced by [MSA Search Pipeline](8-msa-search-pipeline), [Template Search](9-template-search), and [Featurisation and Batching](10-featurisation-and-batching).
- **Downstream**: Its embeddings feed [Diffusion Head](12-diffusion-head), [Atom Cross Attention](13-atom-cross-attention), and [Confidence Head](14-confidence-head).
- **Context**: See [Architecture Overview](7-architecture-overview) for how the trunk fits into the full model pipeline.

# Diffusion Head



The **Diffusion Head** is AlphaFold 3's structure generation engine — a score-based denoising diffusion model that progressively refines noisy 3D atom coordinates into physically plausible structures. Unlike AlphaFold 2's structure module which operated on residue-level frames, AlphaFold 3's Diffusion Head operates directly at **atom granularity**, enabling it to predict coordinates for proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, ions, and modified residues within a single unified framework. The module encompasses four tightly coupled subsystems: a **conditioning network** that fuses Evoformer trunk embeddings with noise-level information, an **Atom Cross-Attention encoder-decoder** that bridges token-level and atom-level representations, a **Diffusion Transformer** that performs the core denoising computation, and an **iterative sampler** that executes the reverse diffusion process at inference time.

Sources: [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L1-L382), [model.py](src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L225-L270)

## Architecture Overview

The Diffusion Head sits downstream of the [Evoformer Trunk](11-evoformer-trunk), consuming its single and pair embeddings as conditioning signals. At inference time, it executes a full reverse diffusion loop — starting from pure Gaussian noise and iteratively denoising across 200 scheduled steps — to produce `num_samples` independent structure predictions (default 5). Each denoising step invokes the full forward pass of the `DiffusionHead` module. The diagram below captures the end-to-end data flow:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Inference["Reverse Diffusion Sampling (200 steps)"]
        direction TB
        NOISE["σ₀ · 𝒩(0, I)<br/>Pure noise at t=0"] --> STEP1["Denoising Step 1"]
        STEP1 --> STEP2["Denoising Step 2"]
        STEP2 --> STEPS["..."]
        STEPS --> STEPN["Denoising Step N<br/>σₙ ≈ 0"]
    end

    subgraph DenoisingStep["Single Denoising Step (DiffusionHead.__call__)"]
        direction TB
        COND["Conditioning<br/>_conditioning()"] --> POSFEAT["Position Feature<br/>Scaling by 1/√(σ²+σ_data²)"]
        POSFEAT --> ENC["Atom Cross-Attn<br/>Encoder"]
        ENC --> ADD["Add trunk_single_cond<br/>Projection + LayerNorm"]
        ADD --> TRANS["Diffusion<br/>Transformer<br/>(24 blocks)"]
        TRANS --> DEC["Atom Cross-Attn<br/>Decoder"]
        DEC --> SKIP["Skip-Connection<br/>Scaling & Output"]
    end

    EVO["Evoformer<br/>Embeddings"] --> COND
    NOISY["Noisy Positions<br/>x_noisy"] --> POSFEAT
    NL["Noise Level σ"] --> COND
    NL --> POSFEAT
    SKIP --> OUT["Denoised Output<br/>skip·x_noisy + out·Δx"]
    STEPN --> FINAL["Final Atom<br/>Positions"]
```

Sources: [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L211-L303), [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L306-L381)

## Noise Schedule and Data Scale

The diffusion process is parameterised by a continuous noise level σ that follows a **power-law schedule**. The constant `SIGMA_DATA = 16.0` is empirically derived from the average atom-position variance across the multimer training set, and it anchors the entire normalisation scheme.

The noise schedule maps a normalised time step `t ∈ [0, 1]` to a noise level:

```
σ(t) = σ_data · (s_max^(1/p) + t · (s_min^(1/p) − s_max^(1/p)))^p
```

| Parameter | Value | Role |
|-----------|-------|------|
| `SIGMA_DATA` | 16.0 | Empirical data standard deviation; anchors input/output scaling |
| `s_min` | 0.0004 | Minimum noise level (final denoising resolution) |
| `s_max` | 160.0 | Maximum noise level (initial noise magnitude) |
| `p` | 7 | Power-law exponent controlling schedule curvature |

At `t=0` the noise level is `σ_data · s_max = 2560` (maximum corruption); at `t=1` it drops to `σ_data · s_min = 0.0064` (near-clean). The high value of `p=7` concentrates most denoising steps at the low-noise regime where fine-grained atomic coordination emerges.

Sources: [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L38-L92)

## Noise Level Embeddings

The noise level σ is injected into the conditioning pathway via **Fourier feature embeddings** with 256 fixed-dimensionality. The embedding pipeline is:

1. **Scale** the noise level by `σ / σ_data` (normalising relative to data scale)
2. **Log-transform**: `z = (1/4) · log(σ / σ_data)`
3. **Affine projection**: `h = z · W + b` where `W ∈ ℝ²⁵⁶` and `b ∈ ℝ²⁵⁶` are **frozen constants** (not learned), originally generated from `jax.random.normal` and `jax.random.uniform` with seed 42
4. **Cosine encoding**: `embedding = cos(2π · h)`

Freezing the weight and bias at compile time ensures deterministic, reproducible embeddings regardless of JAX PRNG implementation changes across versions. The resulting 256-dimensional vector is projected into the single conditioning channel space via a learned linear layer.

Sources: [noise_level_embeddings.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/noise_level_embeddings.py#L20-L151), [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L189-L202)

## Conditioning Network

The `_conditioning` method prepares the pair and single conditioning signals that modulate the Diffusion Transformer's Adaptive LayerNorm. It has a critical training-time feature: **probabilistic dropout** of trunk embeddings (controlled by `conditioning.prob = 0.8`), which forces the model to partially rely on raw atom-level information and improves robustness.

**Pair Conditioning Pipeline:**
- The Evoformer pair embedding is optionally zeroed by `(1 - use_conditioning)` scaling, then concatenated with **relative positional encodings** (relative token index up to 32, relative chain index up to 2)
- A LayerNorm → Linear projection maps to `pair_channel = 128` dimensions
- Two transition blocks (each with GLU-gated feedforward) further refine the pair conditioning

**Single Conditioning Pipeline:**
- The Evoformer single embedding is optionally zeroed, then concatenated with `target_feat` (residue type one-hot, MSA profile, deletion mean)
- LayerNorm → Linear projects to `seq_channel = 384` dimensions
- The **noise level embedding** is projected and added
- Two transition blocks refine the single conditioning

Sources: [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L143-L209), [featurization.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/featurization.py#L145-L200)

## Forward Pass: Denoising a Single Step

The `DiffusionHead.__call__` method implements a single denoising step — the core neural network that maps `(x_noisy, σ) → x_denoised`. The computation proceeds through five stages:

### 1. Input Normalisation
The noisy atom positions are masked and **scaled by the inverse of the combined standard deviation**: `x_scaled = x_noisy / √(σ² + σ_data²)`. This ensures the input has approximately unit variance regardless of noise level, which is critical for stable training across the full noise schedule.

### 2. Atom Cross-Attention Encoder
The scaled positions enter the [Atom Cross Attention](13-atom-cross-attention) encoder, which converts per-token-atom 3D coordinates into per-token activation vectors by running cross-attention over atom subsets. The encoder also injects trunk single/pair conditioning and reference structure metadata (atom types, element, charge, atom names, pairwise distances). It returns both a per-token activation and a skip-connection state for the decoder.

### 3. Trunk Single Conditioning Injection
The encoder's per-token output is augmented with a **projected and layer-normalised** version of the trunk single conditioning, bridging the Evoformer's sequence-level understanding into the diffusion pathway.

### 4. Diffusion Transformer
A **24-block Transformer** with Adaptive LayerNorm (AdaLN) processes the per-token activations. Each block consists of multi-head self-attention (with pair-bias logits from the pair conditioning) followed by a transition block. The Adaptive LayerNorm mechanism uses the single conditioning to compute per-token scale and shift parameters: `output = sigmoid(scale) · LayerNorm(x) + bias`, following the **AdaLN-Zero** design from "Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers" (Peebles & Xie, 2022). The zero-initialisation of the adaptive conditioning projections ensures that each transformer block starts as an identity at the beginning of training.

### 5. Atom Cross-Attention Decoder and Skip Connection
The transformer's output passes through the Atom Cross-Attention decoder, which maps per-token features back to per-atom 3D position updates. The final output applies a **CPSLT-style skip connection** (consistent with the theoretical derivation for denoising score matching):

```
x_denoised = skip_scaling · x_noisy + out_scaling · Δx
```

where:
- `skip_scaling = σ_data² / (σ² + σ_data²)` — attenuates the noisy input at low noise levels
- `out_scaling = σ · σ_data / √(σ² + σ_data²)` — amplifies the correction appropriately

This formulation ensures that at high noise levels (σ ≫ σ_data), the model relies on the learned correction Δx, while at low noise levels (σ ≪ σ_data), it preserves the near-clean input.

> [!TIP]
> The entire denoising forward pass executes within a `bfloat16_context()`, except for the transformer attention logits which are computed in float32 to prevent gradient norm blow-up. This mixed-precision strategy is essential for both numerical stability and TPU performance.

Sources: [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L211-L303), [diffusion_transformer.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py#L32-L186)

## Diffusion Transformer Architecture

The `Transformer` module is a stack of 24 identical blocks, organised into **super-blocks** of size 4 (yielding 6 super-blocks). This organisational pattern enables **rematerialisation** — intermediate activations within each super-block can be discarded and recomputed during backpropagation, trading compute for memory. The pair conditioning is projected to pair-bias logits once per super-block (shared across all 4 internal blocks), amortising the cost of the pair projection.

| Component | Configuration |
|-----------|--------------|
| `num_blocks` | 24 |
| `super_block_size` | 4 (6 super-blocks total) |
| `num_head` | 16 |
| `num_intermediate_factor` | 2 (FFW hidden dim = 2× channels) |
| `block_remat` | False (default; remat at super-block level) |

**Adaptive LayerNorm (AdaLN):** Each attention and transition block normalises its input through a conditioning-dependent affine transform. When `single_cond` is provided: the input is LayerNorm'd without learned scale/offset; the conditioning is separately LayerNorm'd and projected to produce `scale` and `bias`; the output is `sigmoid(scale) · x_norm + bias`. The sigmoid gates ensure the scale remains positive and bounded.

**Adaptive Zero-Init:** Output projections use an additional adaptive gate from the conditioning: `output = sigmoid(cond_gate) · Linear(x)`, where `cond_gate` is initialised with bias −2.0 (so `sigmoid(−2) ≈ 0.12` at init). This makes each block near-identity at training start, dramatically improving optimisation stability for deep architectures.

**Gated Linear Unit (GLU) Transition:** The transition blocks use a **Swish-GLU** activation pattern: `c = swish(a) · b` where `[a, b] = split(Linear(x))`. When `use_glu_kernel=True`, this is dispatched to the `tokamax.gated_linear_unit` fused kernel for performance.

Sources: [diffusion_transformer.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py#L32-L263)

## Reverse Diffusion Sampling

The `sample` function implements the **iterative denoising loop** at inference time. It uses an algorithm closely related to the Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models (DDIM) framework with stochastic noise injection:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Initialise:<br/>x₀ = σ_max · 𝒩(0,I)"] --> B["For each σᵢ in schedule"]
    B --> C["Random augmentation<br/>(rotation + translation)"]
    D["Inflate: t̂ = σᵢ₋₁ · (1 + γ)"]
    C --> D
    D --> E["Add noise:<br/>x_noisy = x + √(t̂² − σᵢ₋₁²) · ε"]
    E --> F["Denoise:<br/>x̂ = denoising_step(x_noisy, t̂)"]
    F --> G["Score estimate:<br/>∇ = (x_noisy − x̂) / t̂"]
    G --> H["Euler step:<br/>x_out = x_noisy + step_scale · Δσ · ∇"]
    H --> B
```

| Parameter | Default | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `steps` | 200 | Number of denoising steps in the schedule |
| `num_samples` | 5 | Independent samples generated per inference |
| `gamma_0` | 0.8 | Stochasticity coefficient for noise inflation |
| `gamma_min` | 1.0 | Noise level threshold below which γ is disabled |
| `noise_scale` | 1.003 | Multiplicative scale on injected noise |
| `step_scale` | 1.5 | Euler integration step size multiplier |

**Key implementation details:**

- **Random augmentation:** At each step, the current positions are subjected to a random rotation (via Gram-Schmidt orthogonalisation of two random normal vectors) and a random translation. This enforces SE(3) equivariance stochastically and prevents the model from exploiting any preferred coordinate frame.

- **Noise inflation:** Before denoising, the previous noise level is inflated to `t̂ = σ_prev · (1 + γ)` where `γ = gamma_0` when `σ > gamma_min` and 0 otherwise. This stochastic inflation improves sample quality by injecting controlled noise, analogous to the stochastic sampler in score-based generative models.

- **Score estimation:** The denoised output is converted to a **score function** estimate: `∇ = (x_noisy − x_denoised) / t̂`. This is the standard relationship between a denoiser and the score (∇ log p) of the data distribution at noise level t̂.

- **Vectorised sampling:** Multiple samples are generated in parallel using `hk.vmap` over the sample dimension, with per-sample RNG splitting. The denoising loop itself uses `hk.scan` with `unroll=4` for XLA compilation efficiency.

> [!TIP]
> The `gamma_min = 1.0` threshold means stochastic noise injection is disabled for the final denoising steps (when σ < 1.0). This is critical: at low noise levels, the structure is nearly converged and additional stochasticity would degrade coordinate precision. The transition from stochastic to deterministic sampling happens automatically at this threshold.

Sources: [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L306-L381), [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L42-L85)

## Configuration Reference

The complete `DiffusionHead.Config` inherits from both `AtomCrossAttEncoderConfig` and `AtomCrossAttDecoderConfig`, unifying all sub-module configurations:

| Config Path | Default | Description |
|-------------|---------|-------------|
| `eval_batch_size` | 5 | Sharding batch size for evaluation |
| `eval_batch_dim_shard_size` | 5 | Dimension sharding for eval batches |
| `conditioning.prob` | 0.8 | Probability of using trunk conditioning (training dropout) |
| `conditioning.pair_channel` | 128 | Pair conditioning output channels |
| `conditioning.seq_channel` | 384 | Single conditioning output channels |
| `eval.num_samples` | 5 | Number of independent samples at inference |
| `eval.steps` | 200 | Number of denoising steps |
| `eval.gamma_0` | 0.8 | Stochasticity coefficient |
| `eval.gamma_min` | 1.0 | Noise threshold for deterministic switching |
| `eval.noise_scale` | 1.003 | Injected noise multiplicative scale |
| `eval.step_scale` | 1.5 | Euler step size multiplier |
| `transformer.num_blocks` | 24 | Diffusion Transformer depth |
| `transformer.super_block_size` | 4 | Blocks per rematerialisation group |
| `transformer.attention.num_head` | 16 | Number of attention heads |
| `per_token_channels` | 768 | Encoder token-level channels |
| `per_atom_channels` | 128 | Atom-level channels in encoder/decoder |
| `per_atom_pair_channels` | 16 | Atom pair channels in encoder |

Sources: [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L95-L131), [atom_cross_attention.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L34-L41), [diffusion_transformer.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py#L192-L198)

## Integration with the Full Model

Within `Model.__call__`, the diffusion head is invoked after the Evoformer's recycling loop completes. The `_sample_diffusion` method partially applies the `DiffusionHead` as a denoising function (fixing `batch`, `embeddings`, and `use_conditioning=True`), then passes it to `diffusion_head.sample` along with a fresh RNG key and the sampling configuration from `config.heads.diffusion.eval`. The resulting `atom_positions` — of shape `(num_samples, num_tokens, max_atoms_per_token, 3)` — are subsequently consumed by the [Confidence Head](14-confidence-head) for per-sample quality assessment and by the structure output pipeline for final coordinate extraction.

Sources: [model.py](src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L249-L353)

## Mathematical Foundations

The Diffusion Head implements a **variance-preserving** denoising framework on continuous-state Markov chains. The key theoretical ingredients are:

- **Forward process:** `x_noisy = x_clean + σ · ε` where `ε ~ 𝒩(0, I)` and `x_clean` has variance `σ_data² = 256`
- **Denoiser–score relationship:** The optimal denoiser `D(x, σ)` satisfies `∇_x log p_σ(x) = (x − D(x, σ)) / σ²`, connecting the network to the score of the marginal distribution
- **CPSLT output scaling:** The skip/output scaling factors derive from the conditional expectation `E[x_clean | x_noisy]` under the joint Gaussian model, ensuring0 ensuring the network learnsF learns a well-conditioned residual
- **Euler–Maruyama integration:** The sampling loop discretises the probability flow ODE `dx/dσ = (x − D(x, σ)) / σ` with first-order Euler steps and optional stochastic perturbation

Sources: [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L295-L303), [diffusion_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L333-L357)

## Next Steps

- **[Atom Cross Attention](13-atom-cross-attention)** — Deep dive into the encoder/decoder that bridges token-level and atom-level representations within the Diffusion Head
- **[Confidence Head](14-confidence-head)** — Understanding how per-sample quality scores are computed from diffusion outputs
- **[Evoformer Trunk](11-evoformer-trunk)** — The embedding pipeline that feeds conditioning signals into the Diffusion Head

# Atom Cross Attention



The **Atom Cross Attention** module is the critical bridge between AlphaFold3's token-level Evoformer representations and its atom-level diffusion module. It solves a fundamental architectural challenge: the Evoformer operates on coarse **token** granularity (one token per residue or ligand atom), while the Diffusion Head must predict coordinates for every individual **atom**. Atom Cross Attention provides the bidirectional information channel—encoding token representations into atom-granularity features via cross-attention, and decoding atom-level refinements back into per-atom coordinate updates—using a carefully designed **encoder-decoder** architecture with skip connections that preserve spatial conditioning across the two passes.

## Architectural Overview

The module decomposes into four tightly coupled stages, orchestrated across two top-level functions—`atom_cross_att_encoder` and `atom_cross_att_decoder`—that share a common `CrossAttTransformer` backbone but differ in their input sources and output projections:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Encoder["atom_cross_att_encoder"]
        A1["Per-Atom Conditioning<br/>_per_atom_conditioning"] --> A2["Layout Conversion<br/>token-atoms → queries"]
        A2 --> A3["Trunk Single/Pair<br/>Broadcast to Queries"]
        A3 --> A4["Pair Conditioning<br/>Offsets + Distances + MLP"]
        A4 --> A5["CrossAttTransformer<br/>(3 blocks)"]
        A5 --> A6["Aggregation<br/>atoms → token_act + skip"]
    end

    subgraph Decoder["atom_cross_att_decoder"]
        B1["Token Feature Broadcast<br/>tokens → token-atoms → queries"] --> B2["Skip Connection<br/>+ encoder output"]
        B2 --> B3["CrossAttTransformer<br/>(3 blocks)"]
        B3 --> B4["Position Update<br/>Linear → 3D coords"]
    end

    A6 -. "skip_connection<br/>queries_mask<br/>queries_single_cond<br/>keys_single_cond<br/>pair_cond" .-> B2

    style Encoder fill:#e8f4e8,stroke:#2d7d2d
    style Decoder fill:#e8e8f4,stroke:#2d2d7d
```

The encoder produces an `AtomCrossAttEncoderOutput` dataclass carrying six fields—`token_act` (aggregated per-token features), `skip_connection` (raw query activations for the decoder), and four conditioning tensors (`queries_mask`, `queries_single_cond`, `keys_mask`, `keys_single_cond`, `pair_cond`) that are **reused verbatim** by the decoder. This skip-connection design ensures the decoder's cross-attention operates with identical geometric and chemical context as the encoder, eliminating information loss from the token-aggregation bottleneck.

Sources: [atom_cross_attention.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L108-L123), [atom_cross_attention.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L126-L360)

## The Atom Layout System

Before examining the attention mechanics, understanding the **atom layout conversion** machinery is essential. AlphaFold3 maintains three distinct atom index spaces, and `atom_layout.convert` with `GatherInfo` objects handles all transitions between them:

| Layout | Shape | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| **token-atoms** | `(num_tokens, max_atoms_per_token)` | All atoms grouped by their parent token; padded to a uniform `max_atoms_per_token` |
| **queries** | `(num_subsets, num_queries)` | Flat atom subsets suitable for cross-attention; each subset contains atoms from neighboring tokens |
| **keys** | `(num_subsets, num_keys)` | Expanded key contexts for each query subset; typically a wider neighborhood than queries |

The `GatherInfo` dataclass encodes gather indices and validity masks for each conversion. The batch field `batch.atom_cross_att` provides five precomputed `GatherInfo` objects that define the complete conversion graph:

| GatherInfo | Conversion | Purpose |
|------------|-----------|---------|
| `token_atoms_to_queries` | token-atoms → queries | Scatter atoms into cross-attention subsets |
| `queries_to_keys` | queries → keys | Expand query context to key context |
| `tokens_to_queries` | tokens → queries | Broadcast per-token trunk features to queries |
| `queries_to_token_atoms` | queries → token-atoms | Gather query outputs back to token-atom layout |
| `tokens_to_keys` | tokens → keys | Broadcast per-token features to keys (derived internally) |

The `atom_layout.convert` function applies these gathers along configurable `layout_axes`, enabling seamless reshaping between the three index spaces without explicit index arithmetic in the attention code.

Sources: [atom_layout.py](/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py#L44-L99), [atom_cross_attention.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L143-L152)

## Per-Atom Conditioning

The `_per_atom_conditioning` function constructs the **single** and **pair** conditioning tensors from the reference structure's atomic metadata. This is the sole source of atom-level geometric and chemical information that bootstraps the entire cross-attention pipeline.

### Single Conditioning

Five atomic features are linearly embedded into `per_atom_channels` (default: 128) and summed:

| Feature | Encoding | Dimensionality |
|---------|----------|---------------|
| **Reference position** | `Linear(positions)` with highest precision | 3 → 128 |
| **Atom mask** | `Linear(mask.astype(float32))` | 1 → 128 |
| **Element** | `Linear(one_hot(element, 128))` | 128 → 128 |
| **Charge** | `Linear(arcsinh(charge))` | 1 → 128 |
| **Atom name chars** | `Linear(one_hot(atom_name_chars, 64).reshape(-1))` | variable → 128 |

The `arcsinh` transform on charge handles the unbounded integer range gracefully. The element one-hot uses 128 classes (covering the periodic table), while atom name characters use 64 classes (ASCII 32–96). The final sum is masked by the atom validity mask to zero out padding positions.

### Pair Conditioning

Pair conditioning captures **intra-token** atom-pair geometry. It is constructed from four additive components, all projected to `per_atom_pair_channels` (default: 16):

1. **Single-to-pair broadcast**: `Linear(relu(act))[row] + Linear(relu(act))[col]` — outer sum of projected single features
2. **Pairwise offsets**: `Linear(positions[i] - positions[j])` with highest precision — encodes relative displacement vectors
3. **Inverse squared distances**: `Linear(1 / (1 + ||pos_i - pos_j||²))` — provides distance-based bias that decays smoothly

These pair conditioning features from `_per_atom_conditioning` are used **only within the encoder** for the initial token-atom pair representations. The encoder subsequently constructs a richer pair representation at the query/key level (described next).

Sources: [atom_cross_attention.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L43-L105)

## Encoder: From Tokens to Atom-Granularity Representations

The `atom_cross_att_encoder` function implements the full encoding pipeline, transforming token-level Evoformer outputs into atom-granularity representations suitable for the Diffusion Head.

### Step 1 — Query Conditioning Assembly

The per-atom single conditioning from `_per_atom_conditioning` is converted from the token-atoms layout to the queries layout via `atom_layout.convert(token_atoms_to_queries, ...)`. If the Evoformer's `trunk_single_cond` is provided, it is projected through a `Linear ∘ LayerNorm` pathway and broadcast from tokens to queries using `tokens_to_queries`, then **added** to the query conditioning. This means each query atom receives both its intrinsic chemical/geometric identity and the Evoformer's learned token-level representation.

### Step 2 — Query Activation Initialization

If `token_atoms_act` is `None` (i.e., at the beginning of the Evoformer trunk before any atom-level iterations), the query activations are set directly to the conditioning: `queries_act = queries_single_cond`. Otherwise, the existing atom activations are converted to the queries layout, projected through a linear layer, masked, and added to the conditioning. This supports **iterative refinement** where Atom Cross Attention is called multiple times within the Evoformer trunk.

### Step 3 — Key Conditioning and Layout Conversion

Key representations are derived by converting query conditioning and masks through `queries_to_keys`. This is a pure layout transformation—no new parameters are introduced—ensuring the key space is a deterministic function of the query space.

### Step 4 — Pair Conditioning at Query-Key Granularity

The encoder constructs a rich pair representation at `(num_subsets, num_queries, num_keys, per_atom_pair_channels)` through six additive components:

1. **Single-to-pair outer sum** from query and key single conditioning
2. **Trunk pair conditioning** — Evoformer pair features projected through `Linear ∘ LayerNorm`, then gathered using a composite `GatherInfo` that indexes into the flattened `(num_tokens × num_tokens)` trunk pair matrix using `tokens_to_queries` and `tokens_to_keys` indices
3. **Pairwise position offsets** between query and key reference positions, masked by `ref_space_uid` equality (offsets are only valid when both atoms share the same reference frame)
4. **Inverse squared distances** between query and key positions, similarly masked by reference frame validity
5. **Offset validity mask** — a learned embedding of whether the offset is valid, allowing the network to distinguish "zero offset because atoms coincide" from "zero offset because different reference frames"
6. **Two-layer MLP residual** — `pair_act += Linear₃(relu(Linear₂(relu(Linear₁(pair_act)))))` that refines the pair representation

> [!TIP]
> The `ref_space_uid` (reference space unique identifier) check is critical for multi-chain complexes: atoms in different chains may have independent reference frames, making their positional offsets meaningless. The `offsets_valid` mask zeroes out invalid offset/distance embeddings, and the separate validity embedding lets the network learn how to handle cross-frame atom pairs.

### Step 5 — CrossAttTransformer and Aggregation

The assembled `queries_act`, conditioning tensors, and `pair_act` are fed into a `CrossAttTransformer` (3 blocks, `num_intermediate_factor=2`). The output is masked and stored as the `skip_connection`. Finally, query activations are projected to `per_token_channels` (768), converted back to the token-atoms layout via `queries_to_token_atoms`, and **aggregated** across atoms per token using `mask_mean` with ReLU activation—producing the `token_act` output that feeds back into the Evoformer.

Sources: [atom_cross_attention.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L126-L360)

## Decoder: From Token Features to Coordinate Updates

The `atom_cross_att_decoder` is the inverse pathway—mapping refined token-level features from the Diffusion Head back to per-atom 3D coordinate updates. Its structure mirrors the encoder but with critical differences in input handling and output projection.

### Step 1 — Token Feature Broadcast

The decoder receives `token_act` at per-token granularity. This is projected down to `per_atom_channels` (128), then **broadcast** to the token-atoms layout by expanding along the atom dimension: `token_act[:, None, :]` → `(num_tokens, max_atoms_per_token, 128)`. The broadcast tensor is converted to the queries layout, where the encoder's `skip_connection` is **added** as a residual. This skip connection injects the full encoder-era atom-level context that was lost during the encoder's token aggregation step.

### Step 2 — CrossAttTransformer Reuse

The decoder runs its own `CrossAttTransformer` (same architecture: 3 blocks, `num_intermediate_factor=2`, but with **separate parameters** named `atom_transformer_decoder`). Crucially, it reuses the encoder's `queries_mask`, `keys_mask`, `queries_single_cond`, `keys_single_cond`, and `pair_cond` **without recomputation**. This design ensures geometric consistency: the decoder's attention patterns are conditioned on the same reference structure and Evoformer pair information as the encoder's.

### Step 3 — Position Update Projection

After the transformer, query activations are masked, layer-normalized (without offset), and projected through a final `Linear(3, initializer=global_config.final_init, precision='highest')` to produce 3D coordinate updates. These are converted back to the token-atoms layout via `queries_to_token_atoms`, yielding the output shape `(num_tokens, max_atoms_per_token, 3)` that the Diffusion Head uses to update atom positions.

Sources: [atom_cross_attention.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L370-L429)

## CrossAttTransformer: The Attention Backbone

Both encoder and delegate to `CrossAttTransformer` from the diffusion transformer module. Each block applies **cross-attention** followed by a **transition block**, with adaptive conditioning throughout:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Q["queries_act"] --> CA["Cross Attention<br/>(queries × keys)"]
    K["keys_act<br/>(gathered from queries)"] --> CA
    PL["pair_logits<br/>(precomputed from pair_cond)"] --> CA
    CA --> ADD1["⊕ residual"]
    ADD1 --> TB["Transition Block<br/>(AdaLN → GLU → AdaZero)"]
    TB --> ADD2["⊕ residual"]
    ADD2 --> OUT["queries_act'"]

    style CA fill:#fff4e8,stroke:#b8860b
    style TB fill:#e8f4ff,stroke:#1e90ff
```

### Cross-Attention Mechanism

The `cross_attention` function implements multi-head attention between query and key sets with adaptive layer normalization (AdaLN) on both sides:

- **Query normalization**: `adaptive_layernorm(x_q, single_cond_q)` — applies LayerNorm then modulates by a learned sigmoid-gated scale and bias from the conditioning
- **Key normalization**: `adaptive_layernorm(x_k, single_cond_k)` — same for keys, allowing asymmetric conditioning
- **Pair bias**: Precomputed `pair_logits` of shape `(num_blocks, num_subsets, num_heads, num_queries, num_keys)` are added to the attention logits, injecting geometric pair information
- **Gating**: Output is sigmoid-gated from a learned projection of `x_q`, following AlphaFold's standard gating pattern
- **Adaptive zero init**: The final projection uses `adaptive_zero_init` which, when conditioning is present, scales the output by `sigmoid(Linear(single_cond))` with bias initialized to -2 (so `sigmoid(-2) ≈ 0.12`), ensuring the cross-attention contribution starts small and grows as training progresses

### Pair Logit Precomputation

A significant optimization: `pair_cond` is normalized and projected **once** to produce pair logits for all blocks: `Linear((num_blocks, num_heads))(LayerNorm(pair_cond))`. This avoids redundant pair processing inside each block, reducing the per-block cost from O(Q·K·C) to O(Q·K·H) where H << C.

### Transition Block

Each block's feed-forward component uses the **AdaLN-Zero** pattern from DiT (Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers): `adaptive_layernorm → GLU → adaptive_zero_init`. The Gated Linear Unit (GLU) splits the intermediate representation, applies Swish to one half, and multiplies element-wise, providing a richer nonlinearity than standard ReLU MLPs.

Sources: [diffusion_transformer.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py#L266-L411), [diffusion_transformer.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py#L272-L337)

## Configuration Reference

| Parameter | Encoder Default | Decoder Default | Description |
|-----------|----------------|-----------------|-------------|
| `per_token_channels` | 768 | — | Output channel dimension for token aggregation (encoder only) |
| `per_atom_channels` | 128 | 128 | Channel dimension for atom-level single representations |
| `per_atom_pair_channels` | 16 | — | Channel dimension for atom-pair representations (encoder only) |
| `atom_transformer.num_blocks` | 3 | 3 | Number of cross-attention + transition blocks |
| `atom_transformer.num_intermediate_factor` | 2 | 2 | MLP intermediate width multiplier |
| `atom_transformer.attention.num_head` | 4 | 4 | Number of attention heads |
| `atom_transformer.attention.key_dim` | 128 | 128 | Total key dimension across heads |
| `atom_transformer.attention.value_dim` | 128 | 128 | Total value dimension across heads |

> [!TIP]
> The encoder's `per_token_channels=768` matches the Evoformer trunk's single representation dimension, ensuring the aggregated `token_act` can be directly added to the trunk's single activations. The `per_atom_channels=128` is intentionally smaller—atom-level representations need less capacity than token-level ones because they primarily encode local geometric detail rather than global evolutionary context.

Sources: [atom_cross_attention.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L34-L41), [atom_cross_attention.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L363-L367)

## Encoder-Decoder Information Flow Summary

The complete data flow through Atom Cross Attention can be characterized as a **bottleneck architecture with skip-conditioned reconstruction**:

| Stage | Input | Output | Key Operation |
|-------|-------|--------|---------------|
| Encoder | `token_atoms_act`, `trunk_single_cond`, `trunk_pair_cond` | `AtomCrossAttEncoderOutput` | Atom conditioning → CrossAtt → Token aggregation |
| Decoder | `token_act`, `AtomCrossAttEncoderOutput` | `position_update (N×A×3)` | Token broadcast → Skip-add → CrossAtt → 3D projection |

The encoder compresses atom-level detail into token-level summaries while preserving full atom-granularity context in the skip connection. The decoder reconstructs per-atom coordinate updates by combining new token-level information (from the Diffusion Head's iterative denoising) with the cached atom-level conditioning. This design ensures that **no atom-level geometric information is lost** across the token bottleneck, while still allowing the Evoformer and Diffusion Head to operate at their preferred token granularity.

Sources: [atom_cross_attention.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L108-L123), [atom_cross_attention.py](/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L370-L429)

## Related Modules

- **[Evoformer Trunk](11-evoformer-trunk)**: Produces `trunk_single_cond` and `trunk_pair_cond` consumed by the encoder; receives `token_act` back from the encoder for iterative refinement
- **[Diffusion Head](12-diffusion-head)**: Consumes the encoder's output and drives the decoder to produce per-atom coordinate updates during denoising
- **[Confidence Head](14-confidence-head)**: Operates downstream on the final atom positions predicted through this module

# Confidence Head



The **Confidence Head** is AlphaFold 3's dedicated neural module for predicting the reliability of its own structure predictions. Rather than producing a single scalar, it outputs a rich set of confidence signals — per-atom pLDDT, per-token-pair PAE and PDE, predicted TM-scores, and experimentally-resolved estimates — that together form the foundation for ranking, filtering, and interpreting model outputs. It operates as a post-hoc evaluator: after the Evoformer trunk produces embeddings and the Diffusion Head samples atomic coordinates, the Confidence Head consumes both to assess how trustworthy the result is.

Sources: [confidence_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L38-L39), [model.py](src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L328-L339)

## Architecture Overview

The Confidence Head follows a **refine-then-decode** paradigm. It first enriches the Evoformer's pair and single representations with geometry-aware features derived from the sampled atom positions, then passes them through a lightweight PairFormer stack, and finally decodes multiple output heads from the refined representations.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Inputs
        EP["pair embedding<br/>[N, N, C_pair]"]
        ES["single embedding<br/>[N, C_single]"]
        TF["target_feat<br/>[N, C_target]"]
        AP["dense_atom_positions<br/>[N, N_atom, 3]"]
        PB["token_atoms_to_pseudo_beta"]
    end

    subgraph Feature_Embedding["_embed_features"]
        LT["Linear(target_feat) → left"]
        RT["Linear(target_feat) → right"]
        DG["dgram_from_positions(pseudo-β)"]
        LD["Linear(dgram)"]
        FE["out = left + rightᵀ + dgram_proj"]
    end

    subgraph PairFormer_Stack["PairFormer ×4 layers"]
        PF1["PairFormerIteration"]
        PF2["PairFormerIteration"]
        PF3["PairFormerIteration"]
        PF4["PairFormerIteration"]
    end

    subgraph Output_Heads["Output Heads"]
        PDE["PDE Head<br/>→ full_pde, average_pde"]
        PAE_H["PAE Head<br/>→ full_pae"]
        TM_H["TM-adjusted PAE<br/>→ pTM, ipTM"]
        PLDDT["pLDDT Head<br/>→ predicted_lddt"]
        EXP["Experimentally Resolved<br/>→ predicted_exp_resolved"]
    end

    Inputs --> Feature_Embedding
    Feature_Embedding --> PairFormer_Stack
    PairFormer_Stack --> Output_Heads
```

The module is invoked once per diffusion sample via `sharded_map`, meaning each independently denoised structure gets its own confidence evaluation. This is critical because different samples can have varying quality, and the Confidence Head's outputs drive the ranking that selects the best prediction.

Sources: [confidence_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L101-L279), [model.py](src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L328-L339)

## Configuration

The `ConfidenceHead.Config` class exposes the following parameters:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pairformer` | `PairFormerIteration.Config` | `num_layer=4` | Inner PairFormer stack configuration |
| `max_error_bin` | `float` | `31.0` | Upper bound for PDE distance error bins (Å) |
| `num_plddt_bins` | `int` | `50` | Number of bins for pLDDT histogram |
| `num_bins` | `int` | `64` | Number of bins for PDE distogram |
| `no_embedding_prob` | `float` | `0.2` | Probability of dropping the structure embedding (training only) |
| `pae` | `PAEConfig` | `max_error_bin=31.0, num_bins=64` | PAE-specific binning configuration |
| `dgram_features` | `DistogramFeaturesConfig` | default | Distogram feature extraction for pseudo-β positions |

The `PAEConfig` sub-configuration mirrors the PDE binning but is independently tunable, allowing PAE and PDE to operate on different error scales if needed.

Sources: [confidence_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L41-L60)

## Internal Pipeline

### Stage 1: Feature Embedding (`_embed_features`)

The `_embed_features` method injects structural information from the sampled coordinates into the pair representation. This is the bridge between the Diffusion Head's output and the Confidence Head's processing:

1. **Target feature projection**: The `target_feat` embedding (containing residue-type and per-atom conditioning information) is projected via two independent `Linear` layers and combined as an outer sum: `left_project(target_feat) + right_project(target_feat)[:, None]`. This creates a token-pair representation from single-token features.

2. **Distogram from pseudo-β positions**: The sampled atom positions are reduced to pseudo-β positions (Cβ for non-glycine residues, Cα for glycine) using `atom_layout.convert` with `token_atoms_to_pseudo_beta`. The resulting positions are fed into `dgram_from_positions`, which computes a binned distance histogram over all token pairs — a structural fingerprint of the sampled conformation.

3. **Combination**: The three components (left target, right target, distogram projection) are summed into the existing `pair_act`, enriching it with concrete geometric information about the sampled structure.

The `pair_mask` (outer product of sequence masks) zeros out padding positions in the distogram before projection, ensuring no information leaks from padded tokens.

Sources: [confidence_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L72-L99)

### Stage 2: PairFormer Refinement

After feature injection, the pair and single activations pass through a **4-layer PairFormer stack**. Each `PairFormerIteration` applies:

- **Single attention** over the token dimension (with pair bias)
- **Pair attention** (triangular multiplicative updates + attention)
- **Single transition** and **pair transition** MLPs

This refinement serves the same purpose as the Evoformer's iterative processing: it allows information to propagate across the representation so that local structural errors can be contextualized within the global fold. The PairFormer re-uses the same architectural building blocks as the main trunk but operates independently with its own parameters.

The entire stack is wrapped in `hk.experimental.layer_stack` for efficient parameter sharing across layers, and executes within a `bfloat16` context for compute efficiency before the outputs are upcast to `float32` for numerical stability in the downstream heads.

Sources: [confidence_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L144-L164)

### Stage 3: Output Decoding

The refined representations are decoded by five parallel heads:

#### Predicted Distance Error (PDE)

The PDE head predicts the per-token-pair distance error between the predicted and ground-truth structures. It applies `LayerNorm → Linear(num_bins)` to the pair activation, then **symmetrizes** the logits by adding the transposed logits: `distance_logits = left_logits + swapaxes(left_logits)`. This ensures the PDE matrix is symmetric by construction.

The logits are converted to a probability distribution via `softmax`, then the expected distance error is computed as `Σ(prob × bin_center)`. The bin centers are linearly spaced from 0 to `max_error_bin` (31.0 Å) with a catch-all bin appended at the end. The result is masked by `pair_mask` and averaged to produce `average_pde`.

| Output | Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `full_pde` | `[N, N]` | Per-token-pair expected distance error (Å) |
| `average_pde` | scalar | Mean PDE over all valid token pairs |

Sources: [confidence_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L166-L200)

#### Predicted Aligned Error (PAE)

The PAE head is structurally identical to the PDE head but uses its own independent `Linear` projection and binning scheme (configured via `PAEConfig`). It applies `LayerNorm → Linear(pae.num_bins)` to produce `pae_logits`, converts to probabilities, and computes the expected error as `Σ(pae_probs × bin_centers)`. Unlike PDE, the PAE logits are **not symmetrized**, making the PAE matrix asymmetric — this reflects the fact that the alignment error from residue *i* to residue *j* differs from *j* to *i* when the optimal superposition changes.

| Output | Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `full_pae` | `[N, N]` | Per-token-pair predicted aligned error (Å) |

Sources: [confidence_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L202-L228)

#### TM-Score Adjusted PAE

The `_get_tmscore_adjusted_pae` method transforms the raw PAE probabilities into TM-score-compatible terms. For each bin, it computes:

```
tm_per_bin = 1 / (1 + (bin_center / d₀)²)
```

where `d₀ = 1.24 × (N - 15)^(1/3) - 1.8` is the TM-score length-dependent normalization factor (from Yang & Skolnick, 2004). The expected TM term is then `Σ(pae_probs × tm_per_bin)`.

Two variants are computed:
- **Global**: Uses the total number of tokens as `N`, producing `tmscore_adjusted_pae_global` for the overall pTM score.
- **Interface**: Uses the number of interface tokens per chain pair as `N`, producing `tmscore_adjusted_pae_interface` for the ipTM score. Interface tokens are computed by identifying same-chain pairs via `asym_id` and counting cross-chain interactions.

This computation is performed **outside** the bfloat16 context for numerical precision, as the d₀ calculation involves fractional exponents that are sensitive to reduced precision.

Sources: [confidence_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L230-L329)

#### Predicted LDDT (pLDDT)

The pLDDT head predicts per-atom local distance difference test scores. It operates on the **single representation** (not pair), applying `LayerNorm → Linear((N_atom, num_plddt_bins))` to produce a per-atom histogram. The bin centers are uniformly spaced in [0, 1] with `num_plddt_bins = 50` bins, and the expected value is scaled to [0, 100]:

```python
predicted_lddt = Σ(softmax(logits) × bin_centers) × 100.0
```

This yields a per-atom confidence score where higher values indicate more reliable local structure. The pLDDT values are stored as B-factors in the output mmCIF files.

| Output | Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `predicted_lddt` | `[N, N_atom]` | Per-atom predicted LDDT score (0–100) |

Sources: [confidence_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L246-L259)

#### Experimentally Resolved

A binary classification head that predicts whether each atom is likely to be experimentally resolvable. It applies `LayerNorm → Linear((N_atom, 2))` to the single representation and takes the softmax probability of class 1. This helps distinguish well-ordered from disordered regions.

| Output | Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `predicted_experimentally_resolved` | `[N, N_atom]` | Probability of being experimentally resolved (0–1) |

Sources: [confidence_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L261-L271)

## Complete Output Dictionary

The `ConfidenceHead.__call__` method returns the following dictionary, which is merged directly into the model's top-level output:

| Key | Shape | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `predicted_lddt` | `[N, N_atom]` | Per-atom pLDDT (0–100) |
| `predicted_experimentally_resolved` | `[N, N_atom]` | Per-atom experimentally-resolved probability |
| `full_pde` | `[N, N]` | Full predicted distance error matrix |
| `average_pde` | `[]` (scalar) | Mean predicted distance error |
| `full_pae` | `[N, N]` | Full predicted aligned error matrix |
| `tmscore_adjusted_pae_global` | `[N, N]` | TM-score weighted PAE (for pTM) |
| `tmscore_adjusted_pae_interface` | `[N, N]` | TM-score weighted PAE (for ipTM) |

Sources: [confidence_head.py](src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L273-L279)

## Post-Hoc Score Derivation

The raw Confidence Head outputs are further processed at inference time in `Model.get_inference_result` to produce the final suite of confidence metrics:

### pTM and ipTM

The **predicted TM-score (pTM)** is computed by taking the per-token maximum of `tmscore_adjusted_pae_global` and averaging: `pTM = (1/N) × max_i(tmscore_adjusted_pae_global[i, j])` for each column j, then averaged. The **interface pTM (ipTM)** restricts the computation to cross-chain token pairs using `asym_id`. For single-chain targets, ipTM is undefined (NaN) and pTM is used instead.

### Ranking Score

The ranking score combines multiple signals:

```python
ranking_score = 0.8 × iptm + 0.2 × ptm
              + 0.5 × fraction_disordered
              - 100.0 × has_clash
```

The **fraction_disordered** term uses windowed relative solvent accessible surface area (rASA, from AlphaFold-RSA) with a cutoff of 0.581, computed via DSSP. The **has_clash** penalty flags structures where any chain has >100 polymer atoms within 1.1 Å of another polymer atom, or >50% of its atoms are clashing.

### Chain-Pair Metrics

Several per-chain-pair aggregations are computed:
- **`chain_pair_pae_min`**: Minimum PAE for each chain pair — indicates the best-aligned residue pair
- **`chain_pair_pde_mean/min`**: Mean and minimum PDE per chain pair
- **`chain_pair_iptm`**: Pairwise ipTM between every chain pair
- **`intra_chain_single_pde` / `cross_chain_single_pde`**: Per-chain intra- and cross-chain PDE, weighted by contact probabilities from the Distogram Head

### Contact-Weighted Ranking

An alternative ranking metric (`ranking_confidence_pae`) is computed as the negative contact-probability-weighted average of the full PAE, providing a ranking that prioritizes correctly predicted contacts.

Sources: [model.py](src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L356-L528), [confidences.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidences.py#L56-L206)

## Confidence Categories

The `ConfidenceCategory` enum classifies%:

| Category | pLDDT Range | Character Code |
|---|---|---|
| **HIGH** | 90–100 | `H` |
| **MEDIUM** | 70–89 | `M` |
| **LOW** | 50–69 | `L` |
| **DISORDERED** | 0–49 | `D` |

These categories are serialized in output JSON and attached to each atom via the `AtomConfidence` dataclass, which maps atom-level pLDDT values (read from B-factors) into categorical labels.

Sources: [confidence_types.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidence_types.py#L47-L92), [confidence_types.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidence_types.py#L96-L157)

## Integration with the Model Pipeline

The Confidence Head occupies a specific position in the AlphaFold 3 forward pass:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Input Batch"] --> Evo["Evoformer Trunk<br/>(+ recycling)"]
    Evo --> Diff["Diffusion Head<br/>(sample coordinates)"]
    Diff --> CH["Confidence Head<br/>(evaluate samples)"]
    Evo --> CH
    Diff --> Dist["Distogram Head"]
    Evo --> Dist
    CH --> Post["Post-Processing<br/>(pTM, ipTM, ranking)"]
    Dist --> Post
    Post --> Output["InferenceResult"]
```

Key integration details:
- The Confidence Head receives **Evoformer embeddings** (pair, single, target_feat) and **sampled atom positions** from the Diffusion Head.
- It is applied via `mapping.sharded_map` with `in_axes=0` over the sample dimension, enabling parallel confidence evaluation across multiple diffusion samples.
- The `asym_id` tensor (chain assignment per token) is passed through to distinguish intra-chain from inter-chain errors for ipTM computation.
- All confidence outputs are merged into the model's result dictionary alongside diffusion samples and distogram outputs.

Sources: [model.py](src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L225-L353)

> [!TIP]
> The Confidence Head's PairFormer stack shares the **same architectural building blocks** as the main Evoformer trunk but uses completely independent parameters. This means it can learn a different distribution of attention patterns specialized for error prediction rather than structure prediction. The 4-layer depth (vs. the Evoformer's deeper stack) reflects that error prediction from already-rich embeddings requires less iterative refinement.

> [!TIP]
> The symmetrization trick for PDE logits (`distance_logits = left_logits + swapaxes(left_logits)`) is a parameter-efficient way to enforce matrix symmetry. Rather than learning a full `[N, N, C]` projection and symmetrizing the output, the model learns a single `[N, N, C]` projection and adds its transpose — halving the parameter count while guaranteeing `PDE[i,j] = PDE[j,i]` by construction. PAE deliberately omits this symmetrization because alignment error is inherently asymmetric.

## Suggested Reading

- For the embeddings that feed into the Confidence Head: [Evoformer Trunk](11-evoformer-trunk)
- For the atom positions it evaluates: [Diffusion Head](12-diffusion-head)
- For how confidence scores are interpreted in output: [Confidence Scores Explained](16-confidence-scores-explained)
- For the full output format containing all confidence fields: [Output Format and Metrics](15-output-format-and-metrics)

# Output Format and Metrics



AlphaFold 3 produces a rich, multi-layered output artifact for every prediction job — from the atomic coordinates in an mmCIF file to per-atom confidence estimates and chain-pair interaction scores. Understanding the structure and semantics of these outputs is essential for interpreting prediction quality, ranking alternative samples, and downstream integration with structural biology tools. This page provides a comprehensive map of every file, metric, and data structure AlphaFold 3 writes, grounded directly in the source code that generates them.

Sources: [output.md](docs/output.md#L1-L249), [confidences.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidences.py#L1-L673), [confidence_types.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidence_types.py#L1-L294)

## Output Directory Structure

For each input job, AlphaFold 3 creates a directory named after the **sanitized** version of the job name — spaces and parentheses are replaced with underscores, while case is preserved. If the directory already exists, a timestamp is appended unless `--force_output_dir` is passed. The output path can also be a Google Cloud Storage URI (`gs://`) if the `gcsfs` dependency is installed.

The following Mermaid diagram illustrates the full output directory tree for a job called `"Hello Fold"` with 1 seed and 5 samples:

```mermaid
graph TD
    ROOT["hello_fold/"] --> T1["TERMS_OF_USE.md"]
    ROOT --> T2["hello_fold_model.cif<br/><i>Top-ranking structure</i>"]
    ROOT --> T3["hello_fold_confidences.json<br/><i>Top-ranking full confidences</i>"]
    ROOT --> T4["hello_fold_summary_confidences.json<br/><i>Top-ranking summary</i>"]
    ROOT --> T5["hello_fold_data.json<br/><i>Input + MSA + templates</i>"]
    ROOT --> T6["hello_fold_ranking_scores.csv<br/><i>All samples ranked</i>"]

    ROOT --> DISTO["seed-1234_distogram/<br/>── distogram.npz"]
    ROOT --> EMB["seed-1234_embeddings/<br/>── embeddings.npz"]

    ROOT --> S0["seed-1234_sample-0/"]
    ROOT --> S1["seed-1234_sample-1/"]
    ROOT --> S4["seed-1234_sample-4/"]

    S0 --> C0["...sample-0_model.cif"]
    S0 --> CF0["...sample-0_confidences.json"]
    S0 --> CS0["...sample-0_summary_confidences.json"]

    S1 --> C1["...sample-1_model.cif"]
    S1 --> CF1["...sample-1_confidences.json"]
    S1 --> CS1["...sample-1_summary_confidences.json"]

    S4 --> C4["...sample-4_model.cif"]
    S4 --> CF4["...sample-4_confidences.json"]
    S4 --> CS4["...sample-4_summary_confidences.json"]

    style ROOT fill:#1a73e8,color:#fff
    style S0 fill:#e8f0fe
    style S1 fill:#e8f0fe
    style S4 fill:#e8f0fe
    style DISTO fill:#fef7e0
    style EMB fill:#fef7e0
```

The directory contains three tiers of artifacts. **Root-level files** provide the single best prediction and its confidences, along with the ranking scores across all samples. **Per-sample subdirectories** (`seed-<seed>_sample-<N>/`) hold the full prediction + confidence output for every individual sample. **Optional per-seed artifacts** — distograms and embeddings — are written only when their respective flags are enabled.

Sources: [output.md](docs/output.md#L5-L83), [post_processing.py](src/alphafold3/model/post_processing.py#L104-L141)

## Core Output Files

Every prediction, whether at the root level or inside a sample subdirectory, consists of three files written by the `write_output` function. This function invokes `post_process_inference_result`, which enriches the raw model output with mmCIF metadata, then serializes two confidence JSON files alongside the structure:

| File | Format | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `<name>_model.cif` | mmCIF text | Predicted 3D coordinates. Compatible with most structural biology tools. B-factor column stores per-atom pLDDT scores. |
| `<name>_confidences.json` | JSON | Full 1D and 2D confidence arrays (pLDDT, PAE, contact probabilities). |
| `<name>_summary_confidences.json` | JSON | Scalar and small-array summary metrics (pTM, ipTM, ranking_score, chain-level summaries). |

The mmCIF file is generated by converting the `InferenceResult.predicted_structure` — a `Structure` object — into mmCIF format, then adding metadata (version, timestamp, model ID) and a legal comment. The per-atom pLDDT values are encoded as B-factors within the mmCIF, making them immediately visible in molecular viewers like PyMOL or ChimeraX.

Sources: [post_processing.py](src/alphafold3/model/post_processing.py#L57-L141), [model.py](src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L79-L149)

## Confidence Metrics Overview

AlphaFold 3 extends the confidence framework from AlphaFold 2 to handle the broader range of biomolecules it predicts — proteins, nucleic acids, small-molecule ligands, and post-translational modifications. The three **core metrics** are pLDDT, PAE, and pTM/ipTM, each with domain-specific nuances:

| Metric | Scope | Scale | Purpose |
|--------|-------|-------|---------|
| **pLDDT** | Per-atom | 0–100 | Local confidence. Predicts modified LDDT considering only distances to polymers. |
| **PAE** | Per-token pair | 0–∞ Å | Relative positional error between two tokens after structural alignment. |
| **pTM** | Global scalar | 0–1 | Overall structure accuracy. >0.5 suggests correct fold. |
| **ipTM** | Global scalar | 0–1 | Interface accuracy between subunits. >0.8 = confident; <0.6 = likely failed. |

**pLDDT** has entity-specific behavior: for proteins it approximates lDDT-Cα but at atom-level granularity; for ligands, modified LDDT considers errors only between the ligand atom and polymer atoms (not ligand–ligand); for DNA/RNA, a wider 30 Å radius is used instead of the standard 15 Å.

**PAE** frames differ by entity type: proteins and nucleic acids use backbone-constructed frames (as in AlphaFold 2), while small molecules and PTMs construct frames from each atom's closest neighbors in a reference conformer.

**pTM/ipTM** are strict for small structures — pTM assigns values <0.05 when fewer than 20 tokens are involved. For these cases, PAE or pLDDT are more informative.

Sources: [output.md](docs/output.md#L86-L131), [confidences.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidences.py#L579-L631)

## Summary Confidences JSON

The `summary_confidences.json` file is serialized from the `StructureConfidenceSummary` dataclass. It contains compact metrics suitable for rapid comparison across many predictions:

| Field | Shape | Range | Description |
|-------|-------|-------|-------------|
| `ptm` | scalar | 0–1 | Predicted TM-score for the full structure |
| `iptm` | scalar | 0–1 | Predicted interface TM-score for all interfaces |
| `fraction_disordered` | scalar | 0–1 | Fraction of protein residues predicted disordered (via rASA) |
| `has_clash` | scalar | 0 or 1 | Whether any chain has significant steric clashes |
| `ranking_score` | scalar | [−100, 1.5] | Composite score for ranking predictions |
| `chain_pair_pae_min` | [C, C] | 0–∞ | Minimum PAE between each chain pair — correlates with binding |
| `chain_pair_iptm` | [C, C] | 0–1 | ipTM restricted to each chain pair (diagonal = per-chain pTM) |
| `chain_ptm` | [C] | 0–1 | pTM restricted to each individual chain |
| `chain_iptm` | [C] | 0–1 | Average interface pTM between each chain and all others |
| `chain_ids` | [C] | string | Chain IDs in same order as all chain-level arrays |

Where **C** = number of chains. The `chain_ptm` field maps to `iptm_ichain` (intra-chain pTM) and `chain_iptm` maps to `iptm_xchain` (cross-chain interface pTM) in the internal computation.

> [!TIP]
> The `chain_pair_pae_min` array is particularly useful for identifying which chain pairs interact — low minimum PAE values between two chains suggest they form an interface, while high values suggest they are independent. This can distinguish binders from non-binders without needing to know the interface in advance.

Sources: [confidence_types.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidence_types.py#L160-L230), [confidences.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidences.py#L485-L560)

## Full Confidences JSON

The `confidences.json` file is serialized from the `StructureConfidenceFull` dataclass and contains the complete 1D and 2D arrays needed for detailed analysis:

| Field | Shape | Description |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| `pae` | [T, T] | Full predicted aligned error matrix. Element (i, j) = predicted error in position of token j when aligned to frame of token i. |
| `atom_plddts` | [A] | Per-atom pLDDT scores on 0–100 scale |
| `contact_probs` | [T, T] | Predicted probability that tokens i and j are in contact (≤8 Å between representative atoms) |
| `token_chain_ids` | [T] | Chain ID for each token |
| `token_res_ids` | [T] | Residue ID for each token |
| `atom_chain_ids` | [A] | Chain ID for each atom |

Where **T** = number of tokens and **A** = number of atoms. The PAE matrix is the primary input for computing pTM and ipTM scores, and the `contact_probs` matrix comes from the distogram head. Both are serialized via a C++ binding (`json_serialize`) for performance on large structures.

The `AtomConfidence` dataclass also exists separately — it pairs each atom's pLDDT with a categorical confidence level derived from the `ConfidenceCategory` enum: **H** (90–100, High), **M** (70–89, Medium), **L** (50–69, Low), **D** (0–49, Disordered).

Sources: [confidence_types.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidence_types.py#L233-L294), [confidence_types.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidence_types.py#L46-L93)

## Ranking Score Formula

The `ranking_score` is the single scalar used to rank predictions across all seeds and samples, with **higher being better**. It is computed in the `get_ranking_score` function as:

```
ranking_score = 0.8 × ipTM + 0.2 × pTM + 0.5 × fraction_disordered − 100 × has_clash
```

For **single-chain structures**, ipTM is NaN, so the formula reduces to `pTM + 0.5 × fraction_disordered − 100 × has_clash`. The weights are defined as module-level constants:

| Component | Weight | Rationale |
|-----------|--------|-----------|
| ipTM | 0.8 | Dominant term — interface confidence is the most informative signal for complexes |
| pTM | 0.2 | Secondary — overall fold quality backup |
| fraction_disordered | +0.5 | Disordered regions are expected to have low confidence; this term avoids penalizing them |
| has_clash | −100 | Severe penalty — clashing structures are essentially unrecoverable |

> [!TIP]
> The ranking score should **only** be used for ranking — not as an absolute quality measure. The `fraction_disordered` and `has_clash` terms distort its interpretability. For assessing specific chain or interface quality, use `chain_ptm`, `chain_iptm`, or `chain_pair_iptm` instead.

The clash detection (`has_clash`) flags a structure as clashing if any chain has >100 polymer atoms within 1.1 Å of another polymer atom, or if >50% of a chain's atoms are clashing. The disorder fraction uses windowed relative solvent accessible surface area (rASA) with a cutoff of 0.581, computed via DSSP.

Sources: [confidences.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidences.py#L56-L206), [confidences.py](src/alphafold3/model/confidences.py#L99-L191)

## Multi-Seed and Multi-Sample Ranking

By default, the model samples **5 predictions per seed** (`num_samples=5`). All samples are written to their respective subdirectories, and the top-ranked prediction (by `ranking_score`) is promoted to the root level. The `ranking_scores.csv` file in the root directory lists the ranking score for every prediction, enabling custom re-ranking.

The ranking flow is illustrated below:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Run N seeds × M samples"] --> B["Compute ranking_score<br/>for each sample"]
    B --> C["Write all samples to<br/>seed-X_sample-Y/"]
    B --> D["Select max ranking_score"]
    D --> E["Promote to root:<br/>model.cif + confidences"]
    B --> F["Write ranking_scores.csv"]
    
    style A fill:#1a73e8,color:#fff
    style D fill:#34a853,color:#fff
    style E fill:#34a853,color:#fff
```

If you are interested in a **specific entity or interaction** rather than the full complex, you should rank by a metric specific to that chain or chain-pair instead of the global `ranking_score`.
